children: Wall Street

the trading week higher, as the Federal Reserve's meeting minutes reaffirmed a hawkish stance, a massive SpaceX deal rattled telecom stocks, and AI infrastructure players faced fresh scrutiny over revenue expectations.

The broader AI sector faced a reality check after OpenAI revised its annualized revenue expectations downward, triggering heavy investor scrutiny over the sustainability of massive
Tech-heavy indexes came under pressure this week amid a wider impact on AI trade. Semiconductor stocks were the notable laggards. However, it benefited the financials sector in general.
State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF
added 1.58% during the week to close at $54.73.
Among megacap stocks, Visa
and Mastercard
led the weekly gainers, adding 6.87% week-over-week to $385.45 and 6.68% to $589.14, respectively.

Visa and Mastercard stocks have been rising after Open USD (OUSD) stablecoin went live. The stocks were gaining despite a credit card legislation making headlines this week, which seeks to boost, well, competition and, in the process, lower the swipe fees that the networks and credit card issuers charge merchants.
The proposed bill leaves the dominant networks with the most to lose.
Wells Fargo

(+3.85% W/W to $83.55) was upgraded to Overweight from Equal Weight at Morgan Stanley ahead of its third-quarter earnings release as balance sheet growth normalizes, funding pressures ease, and net interest margin stabilizes.
The bank was also a top pick at TD Cowen as the investment bank resumed coverage of 16 largecap U.S. banks.
Foreign banks led the losers in the category.
HSBC Holdings
saw a 3.29% retreat to $92.98. The lender is reportedly planning to cut roles across its UK wealth business, and is consulting with staff on the reductions.
Mitsubishi UFJ Financial
was down 1.93% to $22.38.
Among largecap losers, crypto stocks led the pack. IREN
(-15.73% W/W to $35.19), Bitmine Immersion Technologies
(-5.98% W/W to $84.27) were the top decliners.

The reason behind the overall crypto market crash is not only leverage but also macro pressure. Federal Reserve minutes pointed to the possibility of another rate increase this year, while the 10-year Treasury yield continued to surge.
XP
led the gainers with a 49.86% advance to $32.22. Nu Holdings
followed with a 20.03% addition to $16.12. Itaú Unibanco
(+18.28% W/W to $10.16) and Banco Bradesco
(+17.81% W/W to $4.30) were the next on the list.
Brazilian stocks surged as the first round of Brazil's presidential election put Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro firmly in the lead.
Brazil-based Inter & Co
led the midcap stocks, advancing 40.15% from the prior week to $7.68.
Crypto names CleanSpark
(-17.62% W/W to $10.50), Riot Platforms
(-14.42% W/W to $16.89), and MARA Holdings
(-14.07% W/W to $9.65) topped the decliners in the category.
Among smallcap stocks, Bit Digital
(-20.86% W/W to $1.29), HIVE Digital
(+23.81% W/W to $6.76), and Vinci Compass Investments
(+22.12% W/W to $11.54) were the notable movers.
